provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Computer systems review
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify hardware components.
The pupils should be able to label the system unit.

Introduction:
We have learned about computers before. Today we will review what makes up a computer.

Content:
Hardware is the physical parts of a computer you can touch. Software is the programs that tell the computer what to do. The system unit is the main box that holds important parts like the CPU and memory. Just like the engine of a car, it is the brain of the computer.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw a computer system and label parts like monitor, keyboard, mouse and system unit.

Evaluation questions:
What is hardware?
Name three hardware components.
What is inside the system unit?

Summary:
Computer systems have hardware and software working together.

topics.title: Word processing mastery
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to format a document.
The pupils should be able to type an essay with proper structure.

Introduction:
We have used computers to write before. Today we will learn to make our documents look better.

Content:
Word processing is using software like Microsoft Word to create documents. Formatting means changing how text looks-making it bold, changing size, or adding colors. We can also set margins and line spacing to make our essays easy to read.

Class activity:
Pupils will type a short essay about their favorite Nigerian food and format it with proper headings and spacing.

Evaluation questions:
What is word processing?
Name two formatting options.
Why is good formatting important?

Summary:
Good formatting makes our documents look professional and easy to read.

topics.title: Spreadsheets basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify rows, columns and cells.
The pupils should be able to create a simple marks sheet.

Introduction:
We use tables to organize information in our daily lives. Spreadsheets help us do this on the computer.

Content:
A spreadsheet is like a grid with rows (horizontal lines numbered 1,2,3) and columns (vertical lines labeled A,B,C). Where they meet is called a cell. We can put information like numbers or text in cells. A marks sheet helps us record and organize student scores.

Class activity:
Pupils will create a marks sheet for five subjects with columns for names and scores.

Evaluation questions:
What is a row?
What is a cell?
How many columns are in column A to E?

Summary:
Spreadsheets help us organize information in an orderly way.

topics.title: Spreadsheet formulas
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to use the SUM formula.
The pupils should be able to use the AVERAGE formula.

Introduction:
We can make spreadsheets do calculations for us. Today we will learn how.

Content:
Formulas are instructions that help us calculate automatically. The SUM formula adds numbers together. We write =SUM(A1:A5) to add numbers from cell A1 to A5. The AVERAGE formula finds the middle value. We write =AVERAGE(B1:B5) to find the average of cells B1 to B5.

Class activity:
Pupils will create a class data sheet with student scores and use formulas to find total and average marks.

Evaluation questions:
What does the SUM formula do?
How do you write a formula?
What does AVERAGE calculate?

Summary:
Formulas help us do math quickly and accurately in spreadsheets.

topics.title: Presentations
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to design slides with text and images.
The pupils should be able to present a topic to the class.

Introduction:
We have seen presentations in class. Today we will learn to create our own.

Content:
Presentation software helps us create slides to share information. We can add text, pictures, and colors to make our slides interesting. A good presentation has a clear topic, not too much text on each slide, and nice pictures that help explain our ideas.

Class activity:
Pupils will create a 3-slide presentation about Nigerian culture and present it to the class.

Evaluation questions:
What is a presentation?
Name two things you can add to a slide.
Why are presentations useful?

Summary:
Presentations help us share information in a clear and interesting way.

topics.title: Internet research
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to search for information online.
The pupils should be able to cite sources properly.

Introduction:
The internet has lots of information. We will learn to find what we need.

Content:
Internet research means looking for information online. We use search engines like Google to find answers. When we use information from websites, we must cite our sources by writing where we got the information from. This helps others find the same information and shows we are honest.

Class activity:
Pupils will research information about Nigerian national symbols and create a list with sources.

Evaluation questions:
What is a search engine?
Why do we cite sources?
Name one way to find good information online.

Summary:
Good research helps us learn new things and we must always give credit to our sources.

topics.title: Digital drawing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to use drawing tools on a computer.
The pupils should be able to design a class poster.

Introduction:
We can draw pictures using computers. Today we will learn how to do this.

Content:
Digital drawing uses software to create pictures on a computer. We have tools like pencils, brushes, shapes, and colors to make our drawings. A poster is a large picture that shares information or advertises something. Good posters have clear messages and attractive designs.

Class activity:
Pupils will design a class poster about the importance of handwashing using digital drawing tools.

Evaluation questions:
What is digital drawing?
Name two drawing tools.
What makes a good poster?

Summary:
Digital drawing helps us create beautiful designs on the computer.

topics.title: Typing speed
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to use home keys properly.
The pupils should be able to measure their typing speed.

Introduction:
Fast typing helps us finish work quickly. We will practice our typing skills.

Content:
Typing speed is how fast we can type without mistakes. Home keys are ASDF for left hand and JKL; for right hand. We keep our fingers on these keys and move only the needed fingers to type other keys. We measure typing speed in words per minute (WPM).

Class activity:
Pupils will practice typing using home keys and then test their speed by typing a short passage for one minute.

Evaluation questions:
What are home keys?
How do we measure typing speed?
Why is good typing important?

Summary:
Good typing skills help us work faster and more efficiently on the computer.

topics.title: Data and charts
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to create different types of charts.
The pupils should be able to turn data into visual charts.

Introduction:
Numbers can be hard to understand. Charts help us see information clearly.

Content:
Charts are pictures that show data in an easy way. Bar charts use bars to compare amounts. Pie charts show parts of a whole. Line charts show how things change over time. We can create charts from data in spreadsheets to make information easier to understand.

Class activity:
Pupils will collect data on favorite fruits in the class and create a pie chart to show the results.

Evaluation questions:
What is a chart?
Name two types of charts.
Why are charts useful?

Summary:
Charts help us understand data quickly by showing it in picture form.

topics.title: Revision and project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to show their best documents.
The pupils should be able to participate in an ICT exhibition.

Introduction:
We have learned many computer skills. Today we will share our best work.

Content:
We will review what we have learned about word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, and internet research. An ICT exhibition is a show where we display our best computer projects to others. We should explain what we did and what we learned when showing our work.

Class activity:
Pupils will prepare their best computer project for display in a class ICT exhibition.

Evaluation questions:
What is an ICT exhibition?
Which computer skill do you like most?
How do you explain your project to others?

Summary:
Sharing our work helps us learn from each other and celebrate our progress.
